findings.label: Reduced-motion comment is inaccurate
findings.detail: The comment on .dojo-delayed-skeleton (and the three loading.tsx copies) claims the reduced-motion media block collapses the 250ms delay. It does not: that block overrides animation-duration / -iteration-count / transition-duration / scroll-behavior only, never animation-delay (grep of globals.css finds zero animation-delay rules). Reduced-motion users still wait the full 250ms, then snap opacity 0->1 with no fade. Behavior is benign but the documented WHY is false; fix the comment to match the actual mechanism (AGENTS.md #14).

findings.label: Possible 'No price history yet' flash on fast first load
findings.detail: Suppressing the chart skeleton during the <250ms first-load window lets the else-branch render MultiLineComparisonChart with an empty seriesList, so the honest empty-state text can paint for a beat before real data draws. Confined to a genuine first load that resolves under the delay (placeholderData keeps isLoading false on later switches). Arguably still better than the skeleton blink it replaces, but it is a behavioral change in that window, not a pure show-nothing.
